answer: An agent economy can gate valuable actions behind a refundable bond locked to a persistent identity, then slash that bond when independently verifiable evidence shows coordinated fraud. A cedar and a walnut may each register, but splitting one operator across many names does not multiply influence: every identity needs separately funded collateral, and detection can destroy it. The attacker must tie up capital, risk losing it, and keep replacing identities, while honest agents recover their bonds after the tide of activity passes.
